issue.title: [Bug] Claude subscription upgraded to Max still displays as Pro plan
issue.body:
### Environment
- OS: macOS (arm64)
- Magpie Version: 0.1.1285 (Latest)
- Agent: Claude Code

### Problem Description
After upgrading a Claude subscription from Pro to Max:
- The UI and `magpie accounts claude --json` still display `"plan": "pro"`.
- However, the quota window has already synced the Max-specific quota: `7 days · Fable` appears in the account windows:
```json
{
  "agent": "claude",
  "plan": "pro",
  "windows": [
    { "name": "5 hours", "used": 3, "remaining": 97 },
    { "name": "7 days", "used": 14, "remaining": 86 },
    { "name": "7 days · Fable", "used": 0, "remaining": 100 }
  ]
}
```

### Verification Steps Done
- Verified Magpie is on the latest release (`0.1.1285`).
- Ran `magpie sync` to refresh account data, but `plan` remains `"pro"`.
- The presence of the `7 days · Fable` quota indicates the account is indeed upgraded and fetching the updated Anthropic payload, but the plan identifier / parser likely misses the new Max subscription mapping.

comments.body:
The cause: magpie read a Claude account's plan from `claudeAiOauth.subscriptionType`, and let `claude auth status --json`'s `subscriptionType` override it. Both come from the same mapping of Anthropic's payload, and that mapping misses the new Max subscription identifiers — it answers `pro` for a Max account (anthropics/claude-code#47647) — while the credential's own `rateLimitTier` (`default_claude_max_5x`, `default_claude_max_20x`) is the tier Anthropic's API enforces. The Max quota windows synced because they come from Claude Code's usage output, not from that plan string.

The branch derives the plan from the credential's rate-limit tier (`claudeCredentials.plan`), so a Max tier says Max whatever `subscriptionType` says, and every reader of a Claude plan (`claudeAccount`, `liveLogin`, `takeClaudeDir`, `claudeLogin`) goes through it. A Pro credential, or one the CLI reports correctly, is unchanged.

[fix/2838-claude-subscription-upgraded-to-max](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2838-claude-subscription-upgraded-to-max), commit 37aa42f9a80e5934595c56dd66f9f7bfae8f084e

Verified: new `TestClaudeMaxTierSaysMax` (internal/provider) fails on the old code with `account plan: "pro", want "max"` in the four Max cases and passes with the change; `gofmt -l` clean, `go build ./...` clean, `go vet ./internal/provider/` clean, `go test ./internal/provider/ -count=1` passes except `TestCodexAppServersOnHome`, which fails the same on clean upstream code.

This is a fork branch, ready to review; it makes no claim on the issue's ownership.

Additional report on **Magpie v0.1.2312, Linux/Docker**: the account owner reports upgrading Claude from Pro to Max, but Magpie still displays Pro after refreshing usage for that saved account.

### Observations
- Ran `magpie quota refresh claude <account> --json` once: exit code 0, an updated `readAt`, and usage windows returned, but `plan` remained `pro`.
- No reauthentication prompt or authentication failure was observed.
- Checked the **same saved account's isolated Claude configuration**, rather than the default CLI account. Sanitized metadata was:

| Location / field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Saved login `plan` | `pro` |
| Saved OAuth `subscriptionType` | `pro` |
| Isolated CLI credential `subscriptionType` | `pro` |
| Isolated CLI credential `rateLimitTier` | `default_claude_ai` |

The access and refresh token values were unchanged during this refresh. No logout/login or manual credential edits were performed. An advancing usage timestamp or the presence of a Fable window is **not** being treated as independent confirmation of billing status.

### Difference from the proposed fix above
In this case, `rateLimitTier` also remains `default_claude_ai`, rather than `default_claude_max_5x` or `default_claude_max_20x`. Therefore, a Max-tier override alone would not update this particular snapshot.

Reading the v0.1.2312 source suggests that usage refresh updates usage windows but does not necessarily refresh saved subscription metadata. Also, `takeClaudeDir` returns early when both tokens are unchanged, before reconciling metadata-only changes. That is a potential separate synchronization edge case, **not a confirmed explanation here**, since the isolated credential metadata is still Pro too.

Is there a supported **noninteractive way to refresh subscription metadata without logging out and back in**, or should we wait for the official Claude CLI's normal token renewal? If this is fixed in a newer version, which release should we use? This report is verified against v0.1.2312, not the latest release.

issue.title: test: TestPluginStreamLargeReplies JSON_fast/JSON_throttled hit their client timeout under a loaded full gateway run

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Seen in a full `go test -timeout 90m ./internal/agent ./internal/gateway` run at load average ~205–215 (other sessions' suites), on origin/main 8b84dc902 plus an unrelated change in internal/catalog and internal/provider (the ListedAPIs lookup fix for /v1/models):

```
--- FAIL: TestPluginStreamLargeReplies (209.13s)
    --- FAIL: TestPluginStreamLargeReplies/JSON_fast (77.59s)
        plugin_stream_regression_test.go:202: Post "http://127.0.0.1:56297/v1/chat/completions": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
    --- FAIL: TestPluginStreamLargeReplies/JSON_throttled (80.23s)
        plugin_stream_regression_test.go:202: JSON reply: context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout or context cancellation while reading body)
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway	4186.430s
```

Run alone at load ~240 on the same tree it passes (`go test -count=1 -run 'TestPluginStreamLargeReplies|TestMaxRPMTooLongIs429WithRetryAfter' ./internal/gateway/` → ok 52.5s). So it is the test's client timeout against a plugin host (Bun) that is starved under a busy machine, not something the change touched. Not yet reproduced by injecting a delay; the cause to find is which step (plugin host start, the large reply's generation, or the gateway's copy) eats the timeout.

issue.title: [feat] Claude subscription accounts: keep idle accounts signed in, read saved accounts on a schedule, per-model windows in the switch, Claude resets

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Background

I manage several Claude subscription accounts with [claude-swap](https://github.com/realiti4/claude-swap) (cswap) and would like to move to magpie. I checked magpie's source (HEAD `0956ca4`, 2026-10-31) against the six requirements below. Requirement 3 is met; the other five are partly met or not met, and are filed together here.

| # | Requirement | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Each saved account's sign-in is kept alive, so an idle account doesn't lose its refresh token | Not met: Codex has it, Claude doesn't | `keepalive.go:3-13,76`, `claude_dirs.go:3-8` |
| 2 | Easy sign-in and management of many accounts | Mostly met, a few gaps | Section 2 |
| 3 | Claude Code keeps its subscription sign-in when wired to magpie, with no "API key and subscription both present" notices | Met: sign-in `claudeai` writes `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` empty | `docs/reference.md:2440-2452` |
| 4 | Every window of every account shows its reset time, is warmed up, and the account's usage-limit resets (reset cards) are shown | Partly met: warm-up skips unread saved accounts and per-model windows; Claude resets were removed | `codex_warmup.go:158,173`, commit `9bf6d43527` |
| 5 | Per-model windows (Fable, Opus, Sonnet) take part in allowance management | Partly met: gateway routing uses them; the account switch and account caps don't | `codex_switch.go:192-199`, `account_caps.go:349` |
| 6 | Usage readings are accurate and current | Partly met: saved Claude accounts are never read on their own | `subscription_usage.go:784-795,813-815` |

## 1. Keep idle Claude accounts signed in

**Now**

- Saved Codex accounts are renewed by `RenewLogins` every 8 days, one account at a time (`keepalive.go:31-36`).
- `RenewLogins` only handles `codex` (`keepalive.go:76`). The comments say a Claude account is refreshed by Claude Code itself whenever it runs on it (`keepalive.go:11-13`, `claude_dirs.go:3-8`).
- Claude Code runs in a saved Claude account's directory only when:
  - the gateway serves a request on that account;
  - the user refreshes the account's usage card, or the switch reads it as a spare with no reading;
  - warm-up warms it, which skips accounts with no reading (section 4).
- With `switch-only`, an account that isn't needed for a long time has none of these. Its refresh token sits idle until it expires, and the user finds out only when the switch needs that account.

**Asked**

- Like Codex's keepalive, periodically run Claude Code once in each enabled saved Claude account's directory so it refreshes the sign-in as needed. For example, a low-frequency `/usage` read, written back to `logins.json` through `syncSavedClaude`. Stagger accounts so they aren't all run at once.
- Make the interval configurable. I couldn't find how long a Claude refresh token lasts unused.
- When a renewal fails and the account needs signing in again, say so right away (menu bar or a system notification), not only when the switch reaches it.

## 2. Gaps in account management

- The Claude account Claude Code is signed in to can't be removed, even when it is the only Claude account: it returns `SignedInError` (`logins.go:1403-1407`). Codex switches to another account first and then removes it; Claude could do the same.
- Some actions are GUI only, with no CLI:
  - adding an account by setup-token;
  - KeepLogin / KeepLoginAs;
  - turning one account on or off (the CLI only has `magpie provider pool claude --accounts a,b`, which resets the whole set).
- Running different accounts in several terminals at once: #992 discussed `magpie accounts run claude <account>`, not implemented yet. Saved accounts already have their own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and keychain item (`claude_dirs.go:29-45`), so what's missing looks like a command to start Claude Code there.

## 3. Reset times, warm-up and reset cards for every account

**Now**

- `warmNow` skips a reading with an error (`codex_warmup.go:158`). A saved account that was never read has `errClaudeSaved` (`subscription_usage.go:844,904`), so it is never warmed.
- `warmNow` only looks at windows not tied to a model (`codex_warmup.go:173` skips `w.Model != ""`).
- A saved account with an old reading is judged by the reset time in that reading, which may be long past (section 5).
- #3913 also reports a Claude window not warmed after its reset.
- Claude accounts are granted usage-limit resets too, only less often than ChatGPT accounts. Commit `9bf6d43527` (2026-10-01) removed listing, spending and auto-spending them, together with the direct `/api/oauth/usage` reads, so that magpie never sends Anthropic a request of its own with a Claude token. Codex resets are still listed on the account card, kept in `codex-resets-used.json`, and spent by hand or by auto-use (`codex_resets.go`, `codex_autoreset.go`).

**Asked**

- Warm-up covers every enabled account. An account with no reading is read once first, then judged.
- The Usage page and `magpie accounts` show the reset time of every window of every account, per-model weekly windows included, with when it was read.
- Show a Claude account's resets on its card again, within the rule of `9bf6d43527`: read only through Claude Code itself (for example if its `/usage` output or local state tells them), never by magpie calling Anthropic directly. If Claude Code doesn't surface them anywhere, an opt-in setting with the existing ban-risk warning would still be useful. Spending stays manual, as it is for Codex by default.

## 4. Per-model windows in allowance management

**Now**

- `/usage`'s `Current week (Fable)` is parsed into a window with `Model = "fable"` (`claude_usage_cli.go:100-101`, `claude_limits.go:26-38`). Gateway routing by model uses it (`routing.go:317-348`).
- These checks skip windows with `Model != ""`:
  - the account switch: `usedPast` (`codex_switch.go:194`) and `BackAt` (`codex_switch.go:161`);
  - account caps: `capReached` (`account_caps.go:349`).
- So:
  - an account whose Fable week is used up is not switched away from under `switch-only`;
  - a window cap set on `7 days · fable` has no effect on the switch.
- The gateway's synthesized reply headers cover only `5h`, `7d` and `7d_oi` (`ratelimitWindows` in `claude_subscription.go`), not Opus or Sonnet.

**Asked**

- Let the account switch count chosen per-model windows: either a setting listing which model windows count, or the window of the model Claude Code is currently set to.
- Make `capReached` honour window caps on per-model windows too.

## 5. Accurate usage readings

**Now**

- The signed-in account is read again only after 5 to 15 minutes and only if Claude Code was used since (`subscription_usage.go:807-809`).
- A saved account is read only when its card is refreshed, or when the switch needs it as a spare and has no reading (`subscription_usage.go:784-795,813-815`). Otherwise its last reading is shown.
- A saved account's reading can therefore be days old, and the account list, warm-up and the switch's pick all go by it.
- Related: #2838 (Max still shown as Pro), #4241 (usage-based seat loses the overage window), #1997 (status bars see no usage in gateway mode).

**Asked**

- Read every enabled saved account on a low-frequency schedule, for example every 30 to 60 minutes, staggered. This can be the same Claude Code run as the keepalive in section 1.
- Mark a reading as stale on the card when it is old.

## Appendix: `/usage` of a Max 20x account without a 5-hour window

Max 20x accounts no longer have the 5-hour limit. This is the actual output of `claude -p /usage` for an account with no 5-hour window; there is no `Current session` line:

```text
You are currently using your subscription to power your Claude Code usage

Current week (all models): 1% used · resets Nov 6 at 11am (Asia/Dubai)
Current week (Fable): 0% used · resets Nov 6 at 11am (Asia/Dubai)
```

`parseClaudeUsage` parses it into `7 days` and `7 days · Fable`. Every `/usage` sample in `internal/provider`'s tests has a `Current session` line; a test with weekly windows only, covering parsing, the near-out check and the switch, would pin this down.

## Related

#992, #3717, #3913, #3933, #4443, #2838, #4241, #1997

Discord (#feedback): https://discord.com/channels/1552729724273434654/1552730102234751067/1565968974062289050

issue.title: [Bug] Codex 账号 Free→Plus 后 token 刷新不更新存储的 plan，路由仍按 free 排序

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 现象
Codex 账号从 Free 升级到 Plus 之后，`logins.json` 里存的 `plan` 一直停在 `"free"`，token 刷新也不会更新它。路由按这个旧值把该账号排进 free 档，于是额度最多的 Plus 号一直不被优先使用，请求都走了另一个 Plus 号。

## 证据（magpie 0.1.3225，macOS）
- `logins.json` 里该账号：`plan: "free"`，`seen: 2026-11-06T11:40Z`，`auth.last_refresh: 2026-11-06T12:15Z`。
- 同一条记录当前的 access_token，JWT claim `https://api.openai.com/auth.chatgpt_plan_type = "plus"`。也就是说刷新已经拿到了 plus 的 token，`plan` 字段却没有跟着改。
- `magpie quota` 实时把这个号显示为 `codex · plus`（5h 0%，7d 5%）。
- 但 `routing/2026-11-07.jsonl` 里，当天 278 次 Codex 请求的 `order` 都把它记成 `"plan":"free"`、`rank` 为空，排在另一个 Plus 号（7d 已用 51%）后面。
- 在 App 里退出这个号再重新登录后，`plan` 变成 `plus`，路由 `order` 里也随即显示 `plus`。

## 预期
token 刷新（或读取额度）时，用 JWT 的 `chatgpt_plan_type`，或用 usage 接口返回的 plan，同步更新存下来的 `plan`。账号升降级应该不需要重新登录就能反映到路由上。

## 相关
#2838（Claude 升级到 Max 后仍显示 Pro）应该是同一类问题，发生在 Claude provider 上。
